# 🌱 Overview {.unnumbered}

This notebook mirrors the structure of the manuscript and, for every stage, shows the **exact script** that produced the result and the **figure (or table) that goes with it**. It is intentionally runnable top-to-bottom.

> ✍️ **Target journal.** *Journal of Experimental Botany* — plant–pathogen interactions / phenomics.
>
> 🧊 **Frozen encoder.** DINOv2 ViT-B/14 is used **without any task-specific training**; every result below is a geometric or statistical reading of its features.
>
> 📦 **Frozen results.** All reported numbers are read from `frozen/frozen_results.json`, so figures and manuscript cannot drift apart.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A[📸 Leaf images<br/>2,192 images · 257 units] --> B[🧠 Frozen DINOv2 ViT-B/14]
  B --> C1[🌐 Global CLS<br/>768-d]
  B --> C2[🧩 Patch grid<br/>16×16 × 768]
  C1 --> D1[Latent space<br/>PCA · UMAP · PLS-DA]
  C1 --> D2[Temporal trajectories<br/>T1 → T2 → T3]
  C2 --> D3[Spatial phenotyping<br/>Moran's I · heterogeneity]
  D1 --> E[Integration<br/>PLS · RV]
  D2 --> E
  D3 --> E
  F[🌿 Conventional severity<br/>R4PDE palette] --> E
  E --> G[📝 Manuscript]
```

# 2 · Frozen DINOv2 embeddings

For each 224×224 image we read one 768-d **global class-token** vector and a 16×16 grid of **patch tokens** (and 32×32 at 448 px for high-resolution symptom maps). The encoder is held frozen — inference only.

```{python}
#| label: extract-embeddings
#| file: src/04_extract_embeddings.py
```

**Why it matters.** Natural leaf images lie on a low-dimensional manifold; infection is a smooth optical deformation of that manifold, which is why disease reads as a *continuous* path through the embedding space.

![**Figure 1.** Latent-phenotyping workflow and its mapping to the three objectives.](figures/Figure_1.png)

---

# 3 · Attention vs patch-based symptom localization

We compare two candidate "disease-locators": raw transformer attention (rollout) and a **patch-based symptom score** (cosine distance of each patch to the healthy control-patch centroid).

```{python}
#| label: attention
#| file: src/06_attention_demo.py
```

**Result.** The patch score tracks the visible symptom (Spearman ρ ≈ 0.35 across T1–T3) while raw attention does not (ρ ≈ −0.10). We therefore treat attention conservatively — the model looks at the leaf, but we read disease in feature geometry, not in attention weights.

![**Figure 2.** Patch embeddings localize the symptom; attention stays on the lamina.](figures/Figure_2.png)

![**Figure 3.** A continuous latent space with three groups (two accessions + control).](figures/Figure_3.png)

**Reading.** PC1–PC2 capture 15.8 % + 14.6 % of the variance; the three groups occupy distinct but *touching* regions — a continuous manifold rather than isolated clusters.

![**Figure 4.** Latent trajectories: ASC 160 travels farthest, Control the least.](figures/Figure_4.png)

**Numbers.** Net latent displacement T1→T3: **ASC 160 = 0.35**, **CAL 96 = 0.24**, **Control = 0.15**. Permutation *P* = 1 × 10⁻⁴ (ASC vs CAL). Within-group dispersion rises monotonically with disease (PERMDISP *P* = 0.001).

![**Figure 5.** Severity and spatial organization are decoupled — leaves of similar severity can be fragmented *or* aggregated.](figures/Figure_5.png)

**Key observation.** Two inoculated leaves of near-identical severity (17 % and 20 %) show opposite spatial patterns (Moran's *I* = +0.28 vs −0.21). Across the dataset, severity and Moran's *I* vary almost independently.
